source_quote: Cold-adapted breed populations still exhibited measurable atopic dermatitis prevalence linked to shared genetic susceptibility markers.
Large working breeds in northern climate registries sustained moderate hip dysplasia prevalence across screening programs.
Canine visceral leishmaniasis remained endemic across tropical and subtropical regions with measurable seroprevalence in heat-adapted dog populations.
Tropical canine populations showed markedly higher gastrointestinal helminth prevalence than temperate-region comparators.
Brachycephalic and heat-sensitive breeds carried significantly elevated heat-related illness risk in primary veterinary care data.
Heat exposure compounded upper airway morbidity in brachycephalic dogs with pre-existing obstructive airway syndrome.
Otitis externa remained a common presentation in temperate-zone primary care veterinary populations with characteristic bacterial profiles.
Periodontal disease prevalence remained consistent across temperate-region primary-care companion dog populations.
Arctic and spitz-type breeds carried distinct immune-mediated skin disease risk attributable to breed-specific genetic heritage.
Companion dog populations in temperate urban settings showed sustained overweight and obesity prevalence in wellness screening.
